## Statements

- Stated by vendor (meta-models, Choose Muse Wonder or Muse Spark): Muse Wonder is a preview aimed at long multi-file coding, multi-hour agent runs and sub-agent orchestration. Meta points high-volume, latency- or cost-sensitive work at Muse Spark instead.
- Stated by vendor (meta-models, Muse Wonder availability): Muse Wonder Full exists only inside Muse Code on the Power Usage and Maximum Usage plans, and Meta publishes no model id for it. Max effort on muse-wonder-1.0 does not select it.
- Stated by vendor (meta-reasoning, How it works, effort table, none row): Never send reasoning effort none to Muse Wonder; Meta's API answers HTTP 400.
- Stated by vendor (meta-reasoning, Max reasoning on Muse Wonder): Keep max effort on Muse Wonder for problems where a right answer beats speed, such as a concurrency bug or a large migration plan; it reasons longer and bills more tokens.
- Stated by vendor (meta-reasoning, How it works): Reasoning tokens count against max_tokens or max_output_tokens and bill as output, so leave room for reasoning when sizing an output limit.
- Stated by vendor (meta-coding-agents, Set up Codex, model_reasoning_effort): Meta's coding-agent setup runs Muse Wonder at high effort as a sound default and keeps xhigh and max for deeper reasoning.
- Stated by vendor (meta-models, Muse Wonder availability, Standard and Contributor mode): Muse Code subscriptions turn Contributor mode on by default, which lets Meta train on your prompts and code; switch it off in settings before sensitive work.
- Stated by harness (muse-code-configuration, Select a model): Muse Code's configuration page still names muse-spark-1.2 as the default and does not list Muse Wonder yet; pass --model muse-wonder-1.0 to reach it.
